headline: Derivative gains and higher income offset investment losses
summary_short: Annaly's Q2 2026 net income attributable to common stockholders was $781.6M ($1.06 diluted EPS), up from $19.8M ($0.03) a year ago, as earnings available for distribution of $0.79/share again exceeded the $0.75 quarterly dividend.
summary_long: Q2 net income attributable to Annaly rose to $822.7M ($1.06 diluted EPS) from $57.1M ($0.03) a year ago and $282.7M ($0.33) in Q1, driven by a swing to $552.4M of net derivative gains (from a $388.8M loss a year ago), net interest income nearly doubling to $488.2M, and net servicing income up to $157.2M, partially offset by a $318.5M loss on investments. Earnings available for distribution was $0.79/share, again above the $0.75 quarterly dividend — the ninth straight quarter EAD covered the payout. Book value per share rose to $20.15 from $18.45 a year ago; economic leverage was 5.6x. The company raised $447M of common equity via its ATM program during the quarter.

drivers.explanation: Net income improved as derivative positions swung to gains and both net interest income and net servicing income rose, which more than offset a decline in net investment gains.

Higher coupon income from larger average Agency MBS and loan balances, plus increased net servicing income, lifted total income; higher interest expense on larger funding balances partly offset the gain.
The swing to $552.4M of net derivative gains, versus a $388.8M loss a year earlier, was the largest single contributor, alongside higher net interest and servicing income.
EPS growth trails net income growth because weighted diluted shares outstanding rose to 740.3M from 621.1M a year ago, reflecting ATM equity issuance.
Equity grew on retained net income and roughly $447 million of common equity raised through the ATM program during the quarter.
